title: Idea Explorer
outcome: Explore an idea quickly: a vision brief and a first learning experiment, with optional stakeholder, interview and journey work when you want to go deeper.

minimumInputs.help: What is the idea, in your own words? One or two sentences is enough.
minimumInputs.example: An app that lets suppliers see where their invoice is in our approval process.

minimumInputs.help: What do you most want to find out about the idea right now?
minimumInputs.example: Would suppliers actually check a portal instead of emailing us?

minimumInputs.help: Who would use it first, if you know? Leave blank if you are not sure yet.
minimumInputs.example: Small suppliers who send us fewer than ten invoices a month.

minimumInputs.prompt: Idea or need in the user's words
minimumInputs.help: Describe the idea or the need the way you would explain it to a friend.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers keep chasing us by email because they cannot see if their invoice was approved.

minimumInputs.help: What is in and out of scope for this exploration? Rough boundaries are fine.
minimumInputs.example: Invoice status only; payments and contracts are out of scope for now.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Anything not yet known about users, value or metrics is written as a hypothesis to test.
What do you believe is true but have not proven? Write it as a guess you can test.
minimumInputs.example: Suppliers who can see invoice status will stop emailing accounts payable.

minimumInputs.help: How could you test that guess quickly and cheaply? Or describe a test you already ran.
minimumInputs.example: Email ten suppliers a status link for two weeks and count follow-up emails.

minimumInputs.prompt: Distinguish planned work from observed results
minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Planned steps and real results are kept apart, so nothing is reported as done before it happened.

minimumInputs.prompt: Scope plus at least one known affected group/person or explicit candidate group
minimumInputs.help: What is this work about, and name at least one group or person it affects (a guess is fine).
minimumInputs.example: Invoice approval; affects the accounts payable team and approving managers.

minimumInputs.help: What do you want to learn from these interviews?
minimumInputs.example: Why approvers delay invoices and what would make them act sooner.

minimumInputs.help: Who will you talk to? Name the group or role.
minimumInputs.example: Five approving managers from operations and facilities.

minimumInputs.help: What do you already know, and what are the open questions you want covered?
minimumInputs.example: We know approvals take nine days on average; we do not know where the time goes.

minimumInputs.help: Whose journey is this? Name the user or group.
minimumInputs.example: A small supplier submitting their first invoice.

minimumInputs.help: What are they trying to get done, start to finish?
minimumInputs.example: Get an invoice paid without having to chase anyone.

minimumInputs.prompt: Known touchpoints or explicitly hypothetical flow
minimumInputs.help: Which steps or contact points do you know about? If unsure, describe how you think it works and say it is a guess.
minimumInputs.example: Email invoice, wait, chase by phone, receive payment (we think).
